title: Mapping of the supplementary motor area in patients with brain tumors using repetitive navigated transcranial magnetic stimulation
summary:
The supplementary motor areas of the cerebral cortex are significantly involved in the planning and execution of movements and speech. Accordingly, damage to these areas, for example as a result of a tumor in this area, can lead to significant motor or speech impairments. Furthermore, these areas in close proximity to the tumor are at increased risk of damage during surgery. Detailed and individualized preoperative planning can potentially reduce the risk of such damage. The purpose of this study is to establish a protocol for mapping supplementary motor areas in close proximity to the tumor and to investigate the clinical significance of this mapping in patients with a brain tumor. 
One method of stimulating the cerebral cortex is "transcranial magnetic stimulation" (TMS). Here, a magnetic pulse is applied to the cerebral cortex through the skull bone, triggering a circumscribed current flow on the cerebral cortex (induction current). Within the scope of the study, the magnetic pulse can be applied specifically to the motor brain areas with the aid of a navigation system. The application of a stimulus triggers slight movements of the fingers. In addition, the application of a series of stimuli attempts to temporarily disrupt the function of this cerebral cortex area from the outside. This can temporarily and completely reversibly interrupt the execution of a motor or linguistic task. In this way, areas that are central to the execution of movements or speech can be precisely localized and this information can be taken into account for operation planning.

interventions.name: Patients with a preoeprative SMA mapping: For the mapping, TMS bursts (repetitive navigated TMS at 20Hz, 120% RMT, 5 seconds per burst) will be applied over the suspected SMA region while patients perform a finger tapping task. Errors in task performance due to the TMS will be recorded.
Historical controls without preoperative SMA mapping

Healthy subjects with a SMA mapping: For the mapping, TMS bursts (repetitive navigated TMS at 20Hz, 120% RMT, 5 seconds per burst) will be applied over the suspected SMA region while subjects perform a finger tapping task. Errors in task performance due to the TMS will be recorded.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients: Suspected tumor after cranial imaging; localisation within supplementary motor area; age > 18 years; written informed consent
Healthy subjects: age > 18 years; written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Patients: Contraindications for receiving an MRI; contraindications for receiving a TMS measurement; more than one seizure per week; missing consent to participate in this study
Healthy subjects: Contraindications for receiving an MRI; contraindications for receiving a TMS measurement; more than one seizure per week; missing consent to participate in this study; psychiatric or neurologic diseases
